import tiktoken

enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("gpt2")

# Default behavior unchanged
tokens = enc.encode("sample text")
assert isinstance(tokens, list), type(tokens)
print("default:", tokens)

# New behavior
text = "the cat sat on the mat and the cat sat on the mat the the the"
tokens, patterns = enc.encode(text, return_repeated_pattern=True)
assert isinstance(tokens, list)
assert isinstance(patterns, dict)
assert len(patterns) <= 3
print("tokens:", tokens)
print("patterns:", patterns)

# verify counts are correct
from collections import Counter
full = Counter(zip(tokens, tokens[1:]))
for pair, count in patterns.items():
    assert full[pair] == count, (pair, count, full[pair])
assert all(count in set(full.values()) for count in patterns.values())
# top-3 property: every returned count >= every omitted count
omitted = [c for p, c in full.items() if p not in patterns]
if omitted:
    assert min(patterns.values()) >= max(omitted)

# explicit False
r = enc.encode(text, return_repeated_pattern=False)
assert r == enc.encode(text)

# edge cases: empty / single token
t, p = enc.encode("", return_repeated_pattern=True)
assert t == [] and p == {}
t, p = enc.encode("hello", return_repeated_pattern=True)
assert len(t) == 1 and p == {}

# more than 3 distinct pairs -> capped at 3
text2 = "a b c d e f g h i j"
t2, p2 = enc.encode(text2, return_repeated_pattern=True)
assert len(p2) == 3, p2
print("cap ok:", p2)

# works with special tokens
t3, p3 = enc.encode("<|endoftext|>hello", allowed_special="all", return_repeated_pattern=True)
